## Summary

Most of this issue's behaviour already landed on the base through the replay-parity work (`streamKindOf`, `LEGACY_THINKING_ID`, the `_streamKinds` map and the `kind` field on the replayed message schema in `session-message-history.js` / `stream.ts`). This change is the criterion-by-criterion audit plus the pins that were missing. No production code changes.

Trial-Closes: 8282

## Audit of the five acceptance criteria

| # | Criterion | Status on base | Pinned by | Mutation proof |
|---|-----------|----------------|-----------|----------------|
| 1 | Reasoning stream records `kind`; a reply does not | Implemented | `session-message-history-replay-parity.test.js` "tags a reasoning stream kind:thinking..." and "does not tag a reply..."; new `session-history-stream-kind.test.js` test 2 (through the manager's serializer) | Dropping the `kind` spread in `recordHistory` turns 8 tests red across these files, including the first test named above |
| 2 | Pre-field state file restores; `-thinking-` entries classify as reasoning | Implemented, but only tested on a literal (`streamKindOf`) and via `setHistory` | NEW `session-history-stream-kind.test.js` test 1: a hand-written old-format state file through the real `SessionManager.restoreState`, replayed through `sendHistoryEntry` (covers `-thinking-<n>` and ACP `-thinking`, reply and user prompt stay unclassified) | Removing the legacy-id branch of `streamKindOf` turns this test red (and 3 older ones) |
| 3 | Field survives persist and restore, including per-entry truncation | Implemented; only `truncateEntry` was unit-tested, nothing crossed serialize -> restore | NEW tests 2-4: `serializeState` -> JSON -> fresh manager `restoreState`; test 4 uses a 60 KiB reasoning entry under an id the legacy rule would not classify, so only the persisted field can carry the kind through the truncation path | Making `truncateEntry` drop `kind` turns tests 2-4 red (and the existing truncateEntry unit test) |
| 4 | Protocol schema accepts the optional field; older clients ignore it | Schema field exists (`kind: z.string().max(32).optional()` on the message schema). The one existing assertion only checked `success`, and zod strips unknown keys, so deleting the field from the schema stayed green | NEW `schemas.test.js` test: `kind` is retained when present, an unknown future kind is accepted, an entry without it parses with no `kind`, over-long kind is rejected | Deleting the field from the schema turns the new test red |
| 5 | Dropping the flag in `recordHistory` turns the first test red | Confirmed | See row 1 | Actually mutated and observed red (`not ok 1 - tags a reasoning stream kind:thinking and keeps its duration`) |

## What changed

- `packages/server/tests/session-history-stream-kind.test.js` (new): four tests through the real `SessionManager` persist/restore path.
- `packages/protocol/tests/schemas.test.js`: one test pinning the replay `kind` field on the message schema.

## Tests

- New server file: 4/4 pass. Proof of red per mutation (each restored from a backup copy afterwards): see the table above.
- Protocol package: all tests pass. Server custom lints all exit 0.
- Full server suite (no coverage): 21351 tests, 21336 pass; 2 unrelated failures: a loopback dev-preview timeout (passes in isolation, 44/44) and a 200 ms redaction timing budget that fails in isolation on this loaded machine (310 ms); neither file is touched.

Trial-Closes: 8215

## Summary
`isLoopbackHost` classified IPv4-mapped IPv6 hosts by string prefix (`::ffff:127.` / `::ffff:7f`), so `::ffff:7f:1` (0.127.0.1) and the incomplete `::ffff:7f` were reported as loopback.

## What changed
- `packages/server/src/bind-host.js`: the mapped-IPv6 branch now parses the full address with the existing `mappedV6ToV4` helper (from `ssrf-guard.js`) and is loopback only when the embedded IPv4 is in 127.0.0.0/8. No third predicate added; the strict predicate in `connection-locality.js` is private, dotted-only and has different (authorization) semantics, so it was not reused.
- Behaviour kept: `::ffff:127.0.0.1`, `::ffff:7f00:1`, case-insensitivity. Newly also correct: `::ffff:7fff:ffff` and `::ffff:7f00:0001` are loopback; malformed dotted tails (`::ffff:127.`, `::ffff:127.example.com`) and `::ffff:7f00:1:2` are not.
- Bracketed hosts were never handled by this function and still are not.

## Tests
- `packages/server/tests/bind-host.test.js`: pins `::ffff:7f:1` and `::ffff:7f` (false), `::ffff:7f00:1` and `::ffff:127.0.0.1` (true), plus case, 7e00/8000 boundaries, extra hextets and malformed dotted tails.
- Proof of red: with the new tests against the old prefix match, `node --test tests/bind-host.test.js` gave 2 failures (`expected: false, actual: true`) in the short/malformed and malformed-dotted tests; after the fix, 18 pass, 0 fail.

Trial-Closes: 8303

## Summary

Three rules decided which directories a session could use and disagreed: Create with an explicit cwd ran `validateCwdAllowed`, Browse (`list_directory`) was `$HOME`-only, and a blank cwd inherited the configured default cwd with no check. Browse now honours what Create honours, and the New Session dialog explains when its prefilled directory is not browsable.

## Design (decided up front)

- Browse allow-set = `$HOME` + each configured `workspaceRoots` entry (realpath-resolved) + the daemon's default cwd, the last only when it passes `validateCwdAllowed`. `$HOME` stays browsable so the user can navigate toward a root.
- The same credential-directory deny-list and chroxy config-dir block `validateCwdAllowed` applies also apply to Browse, even when a root contains `$HOME`.
- Refusals keep the existing `Access denied: ...` response shape; the text now reads "restricted to the home directory and configured workspace roots". Nothing string-matched the old text (the dashboard matches `^Access denied`).
- A blank cwd on Create keeps inheriting `config.cwd` (no behaviour change). The daemon logs one startup warning, naming the reason, when `config.cwd` fails `validateCwdAllowed`.
- Dashboard: no protocol change. On a fresh open with a prefilled absolute cwd the modal issues a `list_directory` for that directory and, on an `Access denied` answer, shows "This directory is outside the browsable roots; Browse can't open it."

## What changed

- `handler-utils.js`: extracted the shared pieces of `validateCwdAllowed` instead of writing a second allowlist: `resolveCwdPolicyHome`, `credentialDirDenialReason` (deny-list + config-dir layers), `resolveWorkspaceRoots`, `browseBoundaries`. `validateCwdAllowed` and the helpers take an optional `realpath` resolver. Create keeps the JS `realpathSync` (no behaviour change); Browse passes `realpathSync.native`, the resolver the listed path itself goes through, so a boundary and a target are always spelled the same way (on Windows only the native resolver expands 8.3 short names such as `RUNNER~1`).
- `ws-file-ops/browser.js`: `listDirectory` checks the deny-list and the allow-set on the canonical path. Missing paths are still contained via the deepest ancestor and unresolvable paths still deny. On the non-ENOENT failure branch the deny-list runs on the resolved visible ancestor (a walk that cannot finish denies), so `<denied dir>/<file>/x` and `<denied dir>/<missing>/x` answer identically, including through a symlink or a symlinked home. The default cwd is resolved once and the validated resolved value is the boundary. `createBrowserOps` takes `{ getConfig, getDefaultCwd, realpath }`, threaded through `createFileOps` from `WsServer`.
- `server-cli.js`: `warnIfConfiguredCwdRefused` runs inside `createDaemonSessionManager`, the factory the daemon builds its session manager with, so it is driven directly by a test.
- Dashboard store: `addDirectoryListingListener` (backed by `registerDirectoryListingListener` in `message-handler.ts`). Every `directory_listing` reply is offered to registered listeners first, then to the single callback slot.
- `CreateSessionModal.tsx`: the probe registers through that listener API, because path autocomplete takes over the single slot after its debounce and a slow reply (normal over a tunnel) would otherwise be lost. The reply is matched by exact path (a trailing backslash counts as a separator only on Windows-shaped paths). Relative, `~` and `..` prefills are not probed. The listener is removed on answer, close and unmount.
- `docs/architecture/reference.md`: `list_directory` / `directory_listing` rows updated.

Note: because the default-cwd entry is gated on `validateCwdAllowed`, it is always inside `$HOME` or a root today; it is listed explicitly so Browse tracks the gate. Its inclusion is covered by a direct `browseBoundaries` test.

## Tests

New: `browse-workspace-roots.test.js` (29), `server-cli-cwd-startup-warning.test.js` (7), WsServer wiring tests in `ws-server-file-ops.test.js` (3), `CreateSessionModalBrowsableNote.test.tsx` (20), `directory-listing-listeners.test.ts` (3). All use temp dirs and a fake home (`homeOverride`, `CHROXY_CONFIG_DIR` pointed at a temp dir, fixtures resolved with the native resolver). Existing CreateSessionModal test mocks gained the new store action.

Proof of red (each run against the unfixed behaviour or a mutation, then restored):
- Browse tests on the original code: 9 of the first 18 failed with the old home-only denial. Dropping the deny-list from Browse fails 5; ignoring roots fails 4.
- Unresolvable-path probes: skipping the deny-list there, or checking the raw unresolved path, fails the symlinked-home and link-into-`~/.ssh` probes.
- Default cwd resolved twice, or the config-dir block resolved with another resolver, fails the one-resolution and resolver-threading tests; defaulting Browse to the JS resolver fails the native-resolver test.
- Startup warning: deleting the call from the factory fails its behavioural test.
- Dashboard: a slow probe reply (300 ms, real autocomplete hook, fake timers) failed before the listener API; loosening the no-path check, the backslash rule or the skip rule each fails its own test; removing the fan-out in the message handler fails the store tests.

Results: server full suite 21386 tests, 0 fail (13 skipped, as before); dashboard vitest 399 files / 7906 tests pass and `tsc --noEmit` is clean; server lints and ESLint on every touched server file are clean.

response.title: fix(server): Browse honours workspaceRoots and the default cwd

## Summary
The doctor tests `accepts custom port` and `passed is true when no failures` hardcoded ports 59123 and 59124 and relied on nothing on the machine holding them; the first also asserted `pass`, so any listener on that port reddened an unrelated PR. The tests now own the port state.

Trial-Closes: 7815

## What changed
`packages/server/tests/doctor.test.js` only:
- Small helpers bind an OS-assigned port on 127.0.0.1 (`listen(0)`), the same address doctor probes.
- `accepts custom port`: obtains a freshly freed port and asserts `pass` and that the message includes it.
- New: a deliberately held port asserts `warn` (both directions of the pass/warn branch are now covered deterministically).
- `passed is true when no failures`: uses a freed port instead of the literal; new companion test shows a held port is only a warning and does not by itself fail the run.

## Tests
Proof of red: with listeners holding 59123 and 59124, the old test failed (`expected: 'pass'`, `actual: 'warn'` at the `portCheck.status` assertion). The new tests pass with those ports held and without (124/124 in `doctor.test.js` both ways). Mutation: making the port probe always resolve fails both new held-port tests, so the `warn` branch is genuinely guarded. Server lints pass; eslint clean.
